case_title: Ramesh Kumar Soni v. State of Madhya Pradesh
trial_court_outcome: Held that the appellant could be tried only by the Court of Sessions and rejected the application for remission to a Judicial Magistrate First Class; no sentence arose at this stage
high_court_outcome: Criminal revision dismissed; trial court view affirmed
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused committed offences under sections 408, 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code. A crime was registered against the accused on 18 May 2007 at a police station in Bheraghat. The investigation remained pending after the registration. The police had not filed a charge-sheet against the accused by the date on which the relevant amendment to the schedule of offences came into force on 22 February 2008. The judgment does not describe the specific acts alleged against the accused, the identity or nature of any victim, or the material gathered during the investigation. No eyewitness, documentary, medical or recovery evidence is described, and no confession or statement by the accused is mentioned. A charge-sheet was filed later, after the amendment had taken effect. The material available concerns the classification of the offences and the status of the investigation on the relevant date, and the evidentiary questions about the alleged conduct are not addressed in the judgment.
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 02.05.2011; Supreme Court: 26.02.2013. (Crime registered 18 May 2007 per page 7, quote: Crime No.129 of 2007 ... was registered against the appellant on 18th May, 2007)
legal_representation: Accused/appellant: June Chaudhary, Sumeeta Chaudhari, Prabhat Kumar, Anshuman Ashok, Dr. Kailash Chand. State counsel: Not stated
investigation_status: FIR/crime registered 18 May 2007; investigation pending and no charge-sheet filed as of the amendment date; charge-sheet later filed
appeal_history: Trial court: held the case exclusively triable by Court of Sessions and rejected remission; High Court: revision dismissed; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
defence_argument: Police had not filed a charge-sheet and the investigation was pending when the amendment took effect, so the appellant had acquired a right of trial before the Magistrate and the amendment shifting the forum did not apply
legal_principle_applied: A change in forum is procedural and presumptively retrospective; no vested right of forum exists; a case instituted after the amendment is tried in the new forum; the Full Bench decision is overruled only prospectively
precedent_relied_upon: New India Insurance v. Shanti Misra (1975) 2 SCC 840; Hitendra Vishnu Thakur (1994) 4 SCC 602; Sudhir G. Angur (2006) 1 SCC 141; Nani Gopal Mitra AIR 1970 SC 1636; Anant Gopal Sheorey AIR 1958 SC 915; Jamuna Singh AIR 1964 SC 1541; Devrapally Lakshminarayana Reddy (1976) 3 SCC 252; Kamlapati Trivedi (1980) 2 SCC 91; I.C. Golak Nath AIR 1967 SC 1643; Baburam (1999) 3 SCC 362; Harish Dhingra (2001) 9 SCC 550; Sarwan Kumar (2003) 4 SCC 147
other_sentence_order: Clarification that the overruling of the Full Bench decision (2008 (3) MPLJ 311) applies prospectively and does not affect cases already tried or at an advanced stage before Magistrates
